shadows.purpose: Elevate highly active or premium primary actions.

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #00D98B; color: #0A1628; padding: 8px 16px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 10px; transition: background 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #00C47E; transform: translateY(-2px); }

narrative.overview: The PICKLERS design system balances high-end, "Apple-tier" software craftsmanship with the dynamic, active nature of pickleball. It leverages a rich, deep dark mode punctuated by vibrant semantic accents.
keyCharacteristics: Athletic Elegance: Crisp, high-contrast typography and vivid accents against deep, immersive surfaces.
Dimensionality: Strategic use of layered shadows and glow effects to elevate interactive elements.
Snappy Interactivity: Purposeful micro-animations rather than sluggish choreography.

rules.name: The Emerald Restraint Rule
rules.body: The primary accent (#00D98B) is powerful. Use it exclusively for primary actions, active selections, and success confirmations.

rules.name: The Tight Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings must use negative letter-spacing (-0.015em to -0.01em) to feel engineered and locked-in, never loose.

rules.name: The Floating Pill Rule
rules.body: Success and error messages must feel like floating objects, using backdrop-blur-2xl, deep shadows, and subtle tinted borders.

dos: Do use the dark "pill" aesthetic for success and error messages.
Do maintain the 8px spacing scale strictly.
Do use shadow-glow for active, premium focal points.
donts: Don't use generic white/gray cards or heavy iOS-style opaque blurs for toasts and alerts.
Don't use glowing neon blobs unstructured.
Don't use generic, flat, template-like SaaS layouts.
Don't use side-stripe borders as colored accents on cards or callouts.
